briefing.opening: Hello everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for 2026-09-21.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis Warnings and Domestic/International Impacts
sections.content: Recent data indicates a deepening climate crisis, with global atmospheric water vapor reaching an all-time high last month, demonstrating an intensifying vicious cycle of climate change [4]. Domestically, critical infrastructure and ecosystems are under threat, with rising seawater temperatures around nuclear power plants and coastal erosion due to the climate crisis, necessitating an urgent national strategy to enhance coastal resilience [3, 5]. Internationally, climate change is imposing immense costs on labor productivity and directly impacting specific industries, as warned by the tea shortage crisis caused by a sharp decline in tea production and soaring prices [37, 44]. Furthermore, the mass emission of sulfur hexafluoride (SF6), the worst climate pollutant, from China's power grid, and the trend of replacing coal power with fossil fuel-based LNG power, are noted as actions counterproductive to achieving carbon neutrality goals [7, 11]. These situations warn that what was once discussed in science fiction is now manifesting as the reality of climate change, demonstrating that the world is facing the dual challenges of war and the climate crisis [33, 40].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Efforts Towards a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts are underway to transition towards a carbon-neutral society. Seoul's Seongdong-gu district is creating 'Seongdong's Seasons,' a climate-resilient garden, and establishing a 'Garden Testbed' in Jungnangcheon to research plants that respond to climate change [2, 6]. Suwon Special City is conducting carbon neutrality practice education for all generations, from infants to middle-aged adults, encouraging citizen participation. Gimhae City and Uiwang City have also spread a culture of carbon-neutral living practices through Chuseok holiday campaigns and 'Two-Feet Day' events [8, 13, 14, 15]. Active participation from civil society and political circles is notable, including the completion of 'Carbon Neutral Riding' by National Assembly members, the Jeju Mayor's participation in a 'Bicycle Riding' event, and the conclusion of Gwangmyeong City's youth climate corps '2026 Climate Academy' [9, 16, 17, 21]. Notably, the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism is promoting the establishment of a 'Carbon Neutral Support Center' to overcome the climate crisis, demonstrating participation from religious communities. The development of the garden industry has also been suggested as an effective way to achieve carbon neutrality goals [12, 19].

sections.title: 🔋 Expansion of Renewable Energy and Future Energy Transition
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is being emphasized as a core pillar of climate change response. A goal has been set to triple renewable energy capacity to 100GW by 2030, accelerating the transition to an 'electric nation,' and the modernization of the power grid and expansion of renewable energy are expected to drive the growth of the arc suppression reactor market [23, 29]. Domestic companies are actively participating in building renewable energy infrastructure; KEPCO KDN is accelerating renewable energy development in Indonesia, and Hanwha Q CELLS and POSCO are collaborating to create an agri-photovoltaic market [27, 32]. Furthermore, in rural areas, discussions are underway regarding priority grid connection for solar power facilities under 1MW and the introduction of 'bio-income villages,' exploring community-based renewable energy expansion [31]. Saemaul Undong Credit Cooperatives are supporting renewable energy villages and social housing through social solidarity finance, highlighting the ESG performance of the financial sector [28, 30].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Change Response and Awareness Promotion
sections.content: The international community's interest and efforts in responding to climate change are also active. Mamdhani invited global leaders to a summit focused on housing, immigration, and climate change, creating a platform for international discussion [34, 38]. In Central Missouri, citizens advocated for climate change action through the 'PeaceWorks 5K Walk,' and it was confirmed that climate change is also recognized as an important issue among Indiana voters [35, 39]. President Murmu emphasized the need for systematic policies and community participation in climate change response, mentioning a strong policy framework [45, 47]. Meanwhile, an editorial stating that strong government support is crucial for Jeju to achieve its 2035 carbon neutrality goal, along with the suggestion that an optimal combination of nuclear power, SMRs, and renewable energy is essential, indicates the need for deep consideration of energy transition policies [18, 24].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the severity of the climate crisis and the multifaceted domestic and international efforts to overcome it. More proactive and integrated responses are required for a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
